sections.h2: Who records deeds in Tipton County?
sections.html:
Recording is the job of the county's Register of Deeds. The office takes mail at PO Box 626, Covington, TN 38019, with deed questions at 901-476-0204. The county's own page cites Tennessee Code 66-24-101 for the office's main duty, which is recording deeds and other instruments the law requires or allows to be filed.

The page also lists what can be recorded: deeds, powers of attorney, mortgages, marriage settlements, plats and military discharges. The Register also collects and accounts for the fees and taxes that go with each filing. For a home sale, that normally means the deed from seller to buyer and, when the buyer borrows, the lender's mortgage or deed of trust. Both documents go through the same counter and are charged the fees below. Ask the title company or closing attorney who will deliver the documents to the office.

Call the office before a closing to ask for its current hours and whether it accepts electronic filing. Lookup of property records is separate: the Assessor's parcel search is at tiptontn.geopowered.com/PropertySearch.

sections.h2: Why does the history of Tipton County land matter at a closing?
sections.html:
This is the Mississippi River side of Tennessee, a county seated at Covington and cut from Shelby County in the autumn of 1823. Its roads and rail lines tell the story of how land changed hands. Randolph was Tennessee's busiest shipping point around 1830, the Memphis and Ohio line passed through what is now Mason in December 1855, and tracks reached Covington in July 1873.

The 1811 and 1812 New Madrid earthquakes moved the river and left places like Reverie on the Arkansas side. The county's western boundary still follows the old channel, so land near the river is where boundary history matters most. Other incorporated places include Munford, Atoka, Brighton, Mason, Burlison, Garland and Gilt Edge.

A few numbers from the Census Bureau frame the local market:

  • About 25,000 housing units for roughly 62,000 residents
  • Three of every four households own their home
  • A median owned-home value of $240,600 for 2020 to 2024
  • 91.4% of people stayed in the same house for a year, which points to settled ownership

sections.h2: What are the Tipton County recording charges?
sections.html:
The county lists its recording fees on the Register's page, using the standard Tennessee schedule. An ordinary instrument of one or two pages is $10.00, and each page after the second is $5.00. Add a $2.00 data processing fee per document and a $1.00 clerk's fee whenever state tax is paid.

ItemFeeSource
Instrument of one or two pages$10.00Tipton County Register of Deeds
Each additional page after two$5.00Tipton County Register of Deeds
Plat$15.00Tipton County Register of Deeds
Data processing, per document$2.00Tipton County Register of Deeds
Clerk's fee, only when state tax is paid$1.00Tipton County Register of Deeds
Certified copy, per page$1.00Tipton County Register of Deeds
Military dischargeNo chargeTipton County Register of Deeds

For a four-page warranty deed on which state tax is paid, the recording charge is $10 for the first two pages, $10 for the next two, $2 for data processing and $1 for the clerk's fee, a total of $23. A release or assignment added to an instrument costs $5.00 for each one after the first, which matters when a payoff and a new loan are recorded together. UCC fixture filings are $13.00, and UCC filings over 10 pages add $0.50 per page.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax and mortgage tax apply in Tipton County?
sections.html:
The Register's counter also collects two state taxes. One is the realty transfer tax, set at 37 cents for each $100 of the price. The other is the mortgage tax at 11.5 cents for each $100 of debt, and the first $2,000 of debt is exempt. The Tennessee Department of Revenue posts the same rates, which the county's fee list labels the conveyance tax and the mortgage tax.

The numbers add up fast on a typical sale. A home sold at the Census median of $240,600 produces a transfer tax of about $890. A $200,000 loan produces a mortgage tax of $227.70, since the taxable amount is $198,000. Both are separate from the recording fees in the table above.

Who pays which tax is set in the purchase contract and shown on the settlement statement, so confirm it with the closing agent before signing. On a $300,000 sale the transfer tax would be $1,110, and a seller who expects a net sheet to the dollar should see that line in advance. County property tax is a separate matter handled by the Trustee, and the Register does not collect it.

sections.h2: Does recording a deed change who gets the next tax notice?
sections.html:
It can. Each October the Trustee mails the notice to whoever held title on January 1. A deed recorded in time for the September cutoff also triggers a second copy to the buyer. A buyer whose deed lands later may see no bill at all and should call the Trustee at 901-476-0211.

That office also posts the numbers a buyer will care about: a 2026 county rate of $1.3417, residential assessment at 25 percent, interest-free payment through February 28, and monthly interest after that. Before a deed goes to the Register, work through this short checklist:

  • Get the Trustee's status on the parcel for the current year
  • Find out whether a city bill, such as Covington's, is also open
  • Check that the legal description and parcel number match the deed
  • Ask the Register's office how it takes payment of the recording fee and state tax

sections.h2: Which Tipton County office holds which record?
sections.html:
The county's "Where Do I" page sorts common requests by office, which helps when a sale turns up a question that is not a recording matter. The Register handles copies of deeds and plats and the recording of a deed or other document. Other pieces of a sale sit elsewhere:

  • Tax maps, property assessment values and the Greenbelt Program: Property Assessor
  • Paying property taxes: Trustee
  • Tax sale auctions: Chancery Court
  • Rezoning and zoning of county properties: Planning and Development
  • Obtaining a new address: TCECD 911

The Assessor also keeps the parcel history. Its page notes that the Assessor tracks property sales, building permits and zoning changes when updating the roll, so a recorded deed feeds into the Assessor's records. A buyer who needs a corrected mailing address for the tax bill should contact the Assessor at 901-476-0213.

sections.h2: What is the property fraud alert, and who should sign up?
sections.html:
The Register offers a free Property Fraud Alert through its computer vendor. Once an owner enrolls, an email arrives whenever a document is recorded under a name the owner has added. A seller who just closed, or an heir managing a family house, can use it to watch for filings under the old owner's name. The enrollment steps on the county's page are:

  • Have a valid email address ready
  • Go to www.mylandalert.com and click Register in the upper left
  • Accept the terms at the bottom of the page and enter the email address
  • Click the verification link, choose a password, and add the names to watch

faqs.q: Which office accepts a deed for recording in Tipton County?
faqs.a: It goes to the Register of Deeds in Covington. The office mails to PO Box 626, Covington, TN 38019, and answers deed questions at 901-476-0204.

faqs.q: What fees apply when a Tipton County deed is recorded?
faqs.a: The base charge is $10.00 for up to two pages, with $5.00 for every page beyond that, a $2.00 data processing fee, and a $1.00 clerk's fee whenever state tax is paid.

faqs.q: How big is the state tax on a Tipton County sale?
faqs.a: The state charges $0.37 for each $100 of the price, so a $240,600 sale carries about $890.

faqs.q: Does a Tipton County loan carry its own tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The state mortgage tax is $0.115 for each $100 of debt beyond the first $2,000, which makes a $200,000 loan cost $227.70.

faqs.q: Is there a free warning when something is filed under my name?
faqs.a: Yes. The Register sponsors a free fraud alert at mylandalert.com. Once you enroll a name, an email arrives each time a document is filed under it.
